ov: Large rodents covered in sharp quills. The Old World and New World porcupines look alike but aren’t closely related. The largest is the third-largest living rodent, after the capybara and beaver.

why.et: In Kenya, porcupines have become crop pests and are eaten as a delicacy.
why.dg: Its barbed quills pierce skin, stay in and hurt more coming out.
why.ac: Old World porcupines are strictly nocturnal; North American ones often rest in trees on summer days.

rg: Old World porcupines: Italy, West and South Asia and most of Africa. New World porcupines: North America and northern South America.
df: Plants: leaves, twigs, bark, roots, fruit and crops.
fx: New World porcupines climb trees, and some species spend their whole lives in them.
